subject: Computer Networking
title: The Internet of Things
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Internet of Things usable.

hook.text: Your fridge orders milk. Your thermostat learns your schedule. Billions of devices now connect to the internet.

buildup.text: IoT devices use lightweight protocols like MQTT and CoAP to send tiny messages over constrained connections.

discovery.text: By 2025, estimates suggest over 75 billion IoT devices will be online — far more than the human population.

twist.text: Most IoT devices have weak security. Default passwords and no updates make them easy targets for botnets.

climax.text: The Mirai botnet in 2016 hijacked IoT cameras and routers to launch one of the largest DDoS attacks in history.

punchline.text: IoT connects everything. Securing it is the hard part.

quiz.question: What major security event involved compromised IoT devices?
options: The Mirai botnet DDoS attack in 2016

details.summary: The Internet of Things connects billions of everyday objects, from thermostats to industrial sensors, to the internet. IoT expanded networking beyond computers and phones to the physical world, creating new applications in home automation, healthcare, agriculture, and manufacturing.
details.whyItMatters: IoT is extending networking to the physical world. Understanding IoT's networking challenges is essential as the number of connected devices surpasses the number of connected people.
takeaways: IoT connects everyday objects to the internet
Billions of IoT devices now outnumber connected people
IoT creates new security and scale challenges for networks

faq.question: What networking challenges does IoT create?
faq.answer: Billions of devices need addresses, requiring IPv6. Many IoT devices have limited power and processing, needing lightweight protocols like MQTT. Security is critical because compromised devices become attack tools, as the Mirai botnet demonstrated. Scale is unprecedented.

faq.question: How many IoT devices are connected today?
faq.answer: Estimates range from 15 to 20 billion connected IoT devices as of the mid-2020s, with projections exceeding 30 billion by 2030. This already outnumbers smartphones and computers combined. Each device adds traffic, security surface, and management complexity to networks.
